title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
source: canonical Median of Two Sorted Arrays concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The inputs are two arrays of integers, each sorted ascending, in any sizes including empty, with at least one value between them. Return the median of every value combined: the middle value when the total count is odd, or the average of the two middle values when it is even.
constraints: at least one of the arrays is non-empty

examples.explanation: The combined order is 2, 8, 11, 14, 19; the middle value is 11.
The combined order is 4, 7, 9, 21; the median is the average of 7 and 9.

hints: The median splits the combined values in half. A partition of both arrays that puts the correct count on each side pins it down.
Searching the shorter array for its cut position is enough: the longer array follows, since both cuts must total half the count.
A cut is correct when every left value is at most every right value; compare the two bordering values on each side. O(log(min(m, n))) overall.
solution: Partition binary search on the shorter array: choose a cut so that the left sides together hold half the values and every left value is at most every right value. The median falls out of the four bordering values. O(log(min(m, n))) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include one empty array, heavy overlap, and very different array sizes

visible.failNote: count the combined values, not per-array medians
an even total averages the two middle values
